Ex-Parte Judgment

1. The brief facts of the case of plaintiff are that the plaintiff is a Non-Banking Finance Company registered under - 2 - Company Act 1956 and the present case has been filed through its Authorised Representative Mr.
Shivam Singh Rathore authorized vide Board Resolution dated 06.06.2022.
The plaintiff is having profile of financing vehicle and money lending from its above mentioned office.
2. The defendant no.1 is the borrower of loan and defendant no.2 is the guarantor/surety for defendant no.1/borrower.

Both the defendants approached the plaintiff for grant of auto loan of Rs.54,000/- to purchase a two-wheeler from M/s.Umang Motors Sales Pvt. Ltd., Saraswati Vihar,
Delhi.

The plaintiff granted the loan of Rs.54,000/- to defendant no.1 and after deducting Rs.700/-
towards file processing charges, paid a sum of Rs.53,300/- to M/s. Umang Motors Sales Pvt. Ltd. on behalf of defendant no.1.

sentences.text: 1 3. It is further stated that a loan agreement dated 07.08.2018 was signed by both the defendants and defendant no.1 had agreed to pay the said loan amount with interest @ 18% p.a. in 18 equal monthly installments of Rs.3810/- each.
However, defendant no.1 defaulted to pay the monthly installments to the plaintiff as per terms and conditions of said Loan Agreement and Schedule A.
A number of ECS for said monthly installments got bounced from bank account of defendant no.1 and even thereafter, defendant no.1 did not pay the installments.
Therefore, as per the - 3 - ledger account of the defendant, the outstanding loan amount became due.
As per statement of account maintained by the plaintiff, the defendants are liable to pay Rs.2,80,515/- to the plaintiff with interest.

Plaintiff brought the same to the knowledge of defendant no.2.
4.

It is further stated that the plaintiff through its counsel sent a demand notice dated 12.08.2022 to both the defendants which was delivered to the defendants, however, the defendants did not turn up to make the payment which caused wrongful loss to the plaintiff and wrongful gain to the defendants.

5. It is prayed that the suit be decreed in favour of plaintiff and against the defendants for recovery of Rs.2,80,515/- alongwith pendente lite and future interest @ 18% per annum alongwith cost of the suit.
6. Summons of the present suit were issued and duly served upon the defendant no.1 through his father on 30.09.2022 and defendant no.2 on 26.09.2022.
However, on account of non-appearance of the defendants, vide order dated 21.07.2023, the defendants were proceeded as ex-parte.
7. The plaintiff has examined himself and led evidence by way of affidavit Ex.PW1/A in which he has re-iterated the averments made in the plaint.

He relied upon the documents as under :-
- 4 - 1.
Ex.PW1/1 is the Certificate of Incorporation of plaintiff company.
2. Ex.PW-1/2 is Board Resolution.
3. Ex. PW1/3 is Certificate u/s 65B I.E. Act 4.
Ex.PW1/4 is Loan Agreement (OSR) and Ex.PW1/5 is Schedule 'A'.
5. Ex. PW1/6
is Ledger Account.
6. Ex.PW1/7 is Legal Notice and Ex.PW1/8 are postal receipts.
7. Ex.PW1/9 and Ex.PW1/10 are tracking reports.

sentences.text: Thereafter, at request of AR of the plaintiff company, plaintiff's evidence was closed vide order dated 07.10.2023.

I have heard ex-parte final arguments of Ld.
counsel for plaintiff and gone through the record.
9. The plaintiff has filed the suit within the period of limitation.
The loan was disbursed within the territorial jurisdiction of this court.
The transactions between the parties also took place within the jurisdiction of this court.

Thus, this Court has territorial jurisdiction to try the present case.
10.
This Court has gone through the evidence on record.
The testimony of plaintiff remained unrebutted and uncontroverted as the defendants failed to cross-examine plaintiff despite opportunity.
The averments made by the plaintiff have been duly proved by PW-1 by way of - 5 - evidence affidavit Ex.PW-1/A and Loan Agreement Ex.PW1/4 and Schedule 'A' Ex.PW1/5.
There is no reason to disbelieve PW-1 and the documents tendered in evidence by him.
Thus, the plaintiff has proved that the defendant no.1 had availed loan facility from it and has failed to repay the loan as per the Loan Agreement.
The plaintiff has relied upon the ledger account Ex.PW1/6 to show the exact amount payable by the defendants.
A perusal of the same shows that defendant no.1 has paid around nine EMIs towards the repayment of the loan.
The plaintiff has sought recovery of cheque bounce charges of Rs.6500/- and over due charges @ Rs.25/- per day of Rs.2,39,725/- apart from the pending EMI amount of Rs.34,290/-.
A bare perusal of ledger account shows that hefty over due charges have been imposed upon the plaintiff.
It has been argued by Ld. Counsel for plaintiff that the over due charges were in the knowledge of the defendants at the time of taking the loan and signing the loan agreement.

However, in the opinion of this Court, the payment of Rs.25/- per day for every defaulted EMI is in terrorem and is in the nature of penalty as the breach on the part of defendant no.1 in paying the EMIs results into payment of a sum much greater than the sum which ought to have been paid.
The law is well settled that penalty clauses are not enforceable.
Accordingly, the plaintiff is entitled to reasonable compensation for the loss suffered by it due to non-payment of the EMIs by the defendants.
In - 6 - view thereof, the plaintiff is entitled to recover a sum of Rs.40,790/- (Rs.34,290/- towards pending EMIs and Rs.6500/- towards cheque bounce charges).
11. The plaintiff has also prayed for pendente lite and future interest at the rate of 18% per annum.

However, having regard to the prevailing bank rates, ends of justice would be met if the plaintiff is awarded pendente lite interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of institution of the suit till the date of decree and future interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of decree till realization.
